security.title: Use of Obsolete Function
security.description: The code uses deprecated or obsolete functions, which suggests that the code has not been actively reviewed or maintained.

evidence.explanation: In Pet.java, the field birthDate (line 46) is declared as java.util.Date, an obsolete class that has been superseded by the java.time API (java.time.LocalDate) since Java 8. The @Temporal(TemporalType.DATE) + java.util.Date pattern is considered a legacy approach; modern JPA applications use java.time.LocalDate directly. The getBirthDate() (line 77) and setBirthDate() (line 97) methods also expose this obsolete type.

security.title: Use of Hard-coded Password
security.description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.

evidence.explanation: In application.yml (line 25), the OpenAI API key is configured as '${OPENAI_API_KEY:demo}'. The Spring property placeholder syntax ':demo' means that if the environment variable OPENAI_API_KEY is not set, the literal value 'demo' is used as the API key for outbound communication to the OpenAI service. This constitutes a hard-coded fallback credential embedded in the configuration file.
